intro.author: Paul, with Timothy named as co-sender (1:1)
intro.written: About AD 60–62 while Paul was imprisoned, traditionally in Rome; some scholars suggest an earlier imprisonment in Ephesus or Caesarea
intro.audience: The church at Philippi, with its overseers and deacons (1:1), the first church Paul founded in Europe (Acts 16)
intro.setting: Philippi was a Roman colony in Macedonia, settled by retired soldiers and proud of its ties to Rome. Paul had been beaten and jailed there when he first preached (Acts 16:22-24). Years later the church sent Epaphroditus with a gift for Paul in prison; Epaphroditus fell ill and nearly died (2:25-30), and Paul now sends him home with this letter.
intro.purpose: Paul thanks the Philippians for their gift, reports on his imprisonment, urges unity and humility, and warns against teachers who demanded circumcision.
intro.bigIdea: Whatever the circumstances, joy is found in knowing Christ and living for him together.

commentary.t: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS
